quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CEO/CFO): organic net sales were up 19%, driven by the Americas up 46% organically, offset by APAC down 9% and EMEA down 14%. Adjusted operating margin was 23.2%, up 170 basis points from Q4 2024, on operating leverage, productivity and favorable price-cost; adjusted operating profit was $668 million, up 33% and $29 million above prior guidance; adjusted diluted EPS was $1.36, up 37% and $0.10 above guidance. Q4 adjusted free cash flow was $910 million, up 151%, helped by the larger advance payments that came with the larger orders; net leverage exited at 0.5 times and Q4 incremental margins were 31%.
quarterly_data.figure: organic net sales up 19%; adjusted operating margin 23.2% (up 170 basis points); adjusted operating profit $668 million; adjusted diluted EPS $1.36 (up 37%); adjusted free cash flow $910 million (up 151%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 segments and regional outlook (CFO/CEO). Americas: sales up 50% with 46% organic growth on broad-based strength across products and customer segments; adjusted operating profit $568 million, up 77%, margin up 450 basis points; the Americas remain the primary engine of growth and the pipeline keeps growing even after the large Q4 order intake. APAC: sales down 10%, 9% organically, primarily due to macroeconomic conditions in China while the rest of Asia remains strong; adjusted operating profit $49 million at a 9.9% margin, down 270 basis points on volume deleverage; China's soft growth rate is expected to persist in 2026, attributed to a weak general market rather than Western-player dynamics ('we are a Chinese player in China. We are silicon agnostic.'), while India and the rest of Asia are robustly accelerating. EMEA: sales down 8%, 14% organically; adjusted operating profit $111 million at a 22.1% margin versus 26.6% a year earlier, with that margin pressure expected into Q1; but 'the coiled spring is uncoiling' - pipelines expanding, sales cycles accelerating (the Nordics as an example), strong Q4 orders, and a return to sales growth expected in the second half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Americas sales up 50% (46% organic), adjusted operating profit $568 million (up 77%); APAC adjusted operating profit $49 million at 9.9%; EMEA adjusted operating profit $111 million at 22.1% (vs 26.6%)

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2025 results (CFO): adjusted diluted EPS of $4.20, up 47% and $0.10 above guidance; net sales of $10.2 billion with 26% organic growth, $30 million above guidance (Americas up 41%, APAC up 18%, EMEA down 2%); adjusted operating profit of $2.1 billion, up 35%; operating margin expanded 100 basis points to 20.4%, driven primarily by productivity and positive price-cost; adjusted free cash flow of approximately $1.9 billion, up 66%, an adjusted free cash flow conversion of 115%, helped by increased advance payments.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $10.2 billion (26% organic growth); adjusted diluted EPS $4.20 (up 47%); adjusted operating profit $2.1 billion (up 35%); operating margin 20.4%; adjusted free cash flow $1.9 billion (up 66%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 demand (CEO): organic fourth-quarter orders were up 152% year over year and 117% sequentially, strong in all regions and markets; trailing-twelve-month organic orders grew 81% (higher including recent acquisitions); book-to-bill was 2.9 times; the backlog is more than double last year's and up 57% sequentially, and is more elongated into the twelve-to-eighteen-month window. There were 'quite a few large orders' but nothing unusual in pricing or timing incentives - orders are getting bigger as system-level buying plays out on a larger scale. The pipeline has not depleted: it is growing quarter to quarter across all regions and product technologies. Customers' requested lead times on the bigger orders range from twelve to eighteen months, pushing deliveries into 2027 while 2026 is well covered; backlog entries are legally binding purchase orders, very often with advance payment. Management expects 2026 orders to be up and the backlog to continue to build directionally. Disclosure change: Vertiv will no longer report actual orders, orders forecast, or backlog with quarterly earnings (full-year historical sales and backlog disclosure stays in the Form 10-K; quarterly calls will give a market view).
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 organic orders up 152% year over year and 117% sequentially; trailing-twelve-month organic orders up 81%; book-to-bill 2.9 times; backlog up 57% sequentially

quarterly_data.signal: Initial full-year 2026 guidance (CFO/CEO): net sales of $13.5 billion at the midpoint, 28% organic growth, with the Americas at high 30% growth, APAC at mid 20% growth and EMEA flat to down mid-single digits; adjusted operating profit of $3.04 billion and a 22.5% margin at the midpoint, 210 basis points of expansion from operating leverage and positive price-cost while investing in capacity and technology; adjusted free cash flow of $2.2 billion, 17% growth, net of higher tax and increased CapEx. Adjusted diluted EPS: the CEO's prepared remarks give $6.02, while the CFO's guidance section in this transcript prints '$6.20 representing 43% growth at the midpoint'.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $13.5 billion at the midpoint (28% organic growth); adjusted operating profit $3.04 billion; 22.5% margin; adjusted free cash flow $2.2 billion; adjusted diluted EPS $6.02

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 guidance (CFO): adjusted diluted EPS of $0.98, 53% growth at the midpoint; net sales of $2.6 billion, 22% organic growth, with the Americas growing high 30s percent, APAC low 20% and EMEA down in the mid-20% range; adjusted operating profit of $495 million, up 47%, at a 19% margin, 250 basis points of expansion. On an exit-rate basis, Vertiv expects to have materially offset the unfavorable margin impact from tariffs as of the first quarter of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 net sales $2.6 billion (22% organic growth); adjusted diluted EPS $0.98; adjusted operating profit $495 million; margin 19%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity, pricing and cost (CEO/CFO): capital spending steps up to 3-4% of sales in 2026 ('call it 3.5') from the historical 2-3%, and most of it is already in flight - factories are being expanded, a couple of new locations are coming live, more output is being pulled from the existing footprint, and suppliers are working hand in hand to scale with Vertiv. Capacity is designed with a wiggle room of 20-25%, which Vertiv sometimes uses to accelerate growth. Lead times have expanded a little in some product lines but are pretty much on customer and end-market lead time across the majority of products. The CFO says CapEx should normalize around 2-3% of sales and gives no 2027 number yet. Pricing continues to be favorable: 2025 pricing exceeded inflation and the same is expected in 2026, with material inflation mitigated through the pricing mechanism and supplier cooperation. Incremental margins are guided at the lower end of the 30% to 35% range because the capacity investments and their ramp-up put some pressure on them.
quarterly_data.figure: capex 3-4% of sales in 2026 (historical 2-3%); capacity wiggle room 20-25%; incremental margins at the lower end of 30% to 35%

quarterly_data.signal: Thermal chain and technology roadmap (CEO), answering an analyst on post-CES talk that 'Reuben raised racks may not need chillers' and a competitor's proposal of stainless steel chillers displacing CDUs: technology evolution is favorable from a content standpoint; some GPUs can run at higher temperatures, as has been true for many of the more recent chips of NVIDIA, but heat rejection will continue to exist and the same data centers carry loads needing lower temperatures, so Vertiv thinks more and more about a hybrid cooling and thermal chain - the number of chillers can fall depending on climate and loads, but not the net number of heat rejection technologies. Vertiv's trim cooler, a chiller optimized to operate at high temperatures with flexibility for lower temperatures that maximizes free cooling, is now a cataloged product. Cooling chips directly other than through a CDU would mostly be niche and, in most cases, 'too dangerous' (the blast radius is too big), so CDUs in various shapes and forms are a long-term element of the thermal chain. Roadmap: Vertiv's technology must land well ahead of the most advanced silicon, so with NVIDIA or other silicon technology providers it looks out two, three years or beyond, and it architects technology with many customers one to three years out. On content per megawatt, the CEO says the analyst's dollar-per-megawatt framework can be used for now, and technology complexity is, if anything, good for TAM per megawatt.

Services (CEO): life cycle services orders grew north of 25% year on year, and the field service headcount is approaching 5,000 people, with field capacity following delivery capacity as the installed base grows (commissioning and start-up are key events). The PerchRight acquisition (as printed in this transcript) strengthens end-to-end fluid management across both the primary and secondary fluid networks - critical systems in chilled water and liquid-cooled AI data centers - from initial design through commissioning and decades of operation, and Vertiv expects to scale that expertise globally through its existing services network.
quarterly_data.figure: life cycle services orders growth north of 25%; approaching 5,000 field people

quarterly_data.signal: Converged prefabricated systems (CEO/CFO): at hundreds of kilowatts per rack, the mechanical, electrical and IT stack must be treated as one system. OneCore is a complete converged, end-to-end data center infrastructure that can scale to gigawatts in 12.5 megawatts building blocks - 'Our collaboration with Hut 8 demonstrates this path.' SmartRun, a converged prefabricated white space infrastructure solution that is flexible across multiple generations of silicon and can be standalone or part of OneCore, is being deployed across several large customers at scale, and 'now work with Compass data centers perfectly shows those capabilities'. Management says system-level orders - the entire powertrain and the entire thermal chain designed to work together - are accelerating, starting to be quite broadly adopted, and are making orders bigger than in the past.
quarterly_data.figure: OneCore scales to gigawatts in 12.5 megawatts building blocks
